audits.text:
## 4b1982424dc1

**Source audited.** Generator SHA-256
`38f4e9ce295c6831193be67afd43f8e85e627fd5aee6d956d44bf5f013791344`
(version 2.0.0). No target files were changed.

**Finding.** The rival **“extend every horizontal cyan run of length at least
3”** fits all three canonical demonstrations.  The intended rule extends only
connected components that are exactly horizontal length 3.  Although the
summary and invariants advertise longer horizontal bars as distractors, the
ordinary generator always adds a fixed vertical length-2 distractor and no
longer horizontal bar.  Across 3,000 production draws (easy/default/hard × 100
seeds × 10 sample indices), zero horizontal components longer than 3 appeared;
only three component-type multisets occurred.

A 7×10 documented-domain input containing one exact length-3 bar and one
length-4 distractor passes `self_check([])`.  The Racket authority extends only
the length-3 bar.  The rival additionally paints row 4, columns 2 and 7, producing
two exact disagreements.  The witness is validator-accepted and matches the
documented distractor domain, but it is **not** claimed to be emitted by the
current ordinary production sampler.  Full grids, scan denominator, outputs,
and differing cells are in
`checks/audit/4b1982424dc1/counterexample.json`.

Authority command (workspace root):

```text
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 4b1982424dc1 \
  --input ../checks/audit/4b1982424dc1/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/4b1982424dc1/racket.json
```

The receipt records executed rule hash `f2340cb4b06f` and matching catalog
identity.  The repair direction is to emit longer horizontal distractors in
ordinary lessons; this audit intentionally does not modify the target.
